newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE says Belarus failed to restore democracy.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says Belarus failed to restore democracy.

text.p: Europe's top security body on Thursday said Belarus had failed to restore democracy despite repeated calls by the West to President Alexander Lukashenko to end the crisis in the former Soviet Republic.

"Unfortunately, the situation has not improved," said Niels Helveg Petersen, Danish Foreign Minister and chairman-in-office of the Vienna-based Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

"I therefore urge once again the government of Belarus to take action to respect its commitments to OSCE norms and principles, to enter into dialogue with the opposition and to ensure freedom of media and not restrict access to the media for members of the opposition," he told the OSCE's permanent council in a speech.

In December, the OSCE summit in Lisbon called on Belarus to restore democracy and respect the constitution after a nationwide referendum which Lukashenko used to enhance his powers at the expense of parliament.
Petersen reiterated that the 54-member OSCE was willing to cooperate with Belarus "in overcoming deficiencies within the constitutional area".
The European Union urged Lukashenko in December to fully respect democracy and accept a fact-finding mission, warning relations would otherwise suffer.
